papers.title: When evidence meets artificial intelligence.
papers.one_line: Reviews how artificial intelligence extends evidence generation through multimodal data integration, trial emulation and simulation, while insisting that predictive performance does not establish causal validity or clinical benefit.
papers.what_was_done: Evidence-based medicine as defined by Sackett brought clinical expertise, patient preferences and empirical evidence together, and three decades on faces limited generalizability of trials against the scale and heterogeneity of contemporary health systems. The review positions artificial intelligence as an extension of epidemiologic reasoning rather than a replacement, examining multimodal data integration, target trial emulation and simulation-based modelling as the routes by which computational capacity broadens the reach of systematic observation and critical appraisal. Its central caution is that analytic sophistication does not deliver causal validity or equitable impact, so responsible adoption requires rigorous epidemiologic design, transparent validation, attention to data provenance and bias, and governance structures independent of commercial or institutional pressure. Implementation is framed as depending on integration within clinical informatics systems and on human-machine collaboration, with clinicians retaining the ability to interrogate, contextualize and challenge algorithmic recommendations. For the Americas specifically the review notes that fragmented health systems and uneven digital infrastructure constrain representativeness and equitable deployment, so the technology could reinforce existing inequities without structural change.

future_research.gap: Governance reform, transparent validation and structural change are prerequisites without which these methods would reinforce existing inequities.
future_research.quote: AI will not transform EBM on its own; its constructive role requires governance reform, transparent validation, and structural change to prevent the reinforcement of existing inequities.

problems.evidence: The review's repeated point is that predictive accuracy and causal validity are different properties, and that flexible computational methods deliver the first without touching the second. It places emulation among the tools whose value depends on epidemiologic design rather than on the modelling capacity behind them.
problems.quote: Yet analytic sophistication does not guarantee causal validity or equitable impact.

problems.evidence: Representativeness is identified as constrained by fragmented health systems and uneven digital infrastructure rather than by any analytic choice, which makes the fitness of the data a property of the health system that produced it. The review names data provenance as requiring sustained attention without stating what would be checked.
problems.quote: In the Americas, fragmented health systems and uneven digital infrastructures constrain representativeness and equitable deployment.

papers.title: Bringing credibility to observational research in critical care: the case of target trial emulation designs.
papers.one_line: Gives critical care clinicians three questions for judging an emulation, clarity of the causal question and target trial, alignment of eligibility, assignment and follow-up start, and whether the data cover the confounders, and argues the framework's main contribution is reducing ambiguity about what is being asked.
papers.what_was_done: The viewpoint opens with the field's historical position that causal language does not belong in observational work, against which trials in critical care have often produced negative results or findings not confirmed later, one leading explanation being that the population enrolled in critical care trials is not the population that would benefit or that receives the therapy in practice. Statistical methods from epidemiology and econometrics combined with large databases have changed what observational studies can support. The framework is presented through three appraisal questions. First, whether the authors state the causal question and specify the target trial being emulated, on the argument that the framework's most impactful contribution is reducing ambiguity about causal questions because valid answers are impossible without knowing the question, and that specifying the trial also surfaces the sources of bias. Second, whether the time points for eligibility ascertainment, treatment assignment and start of follow-up are properly aligned. Third, the quality of the data and the extent to which the available variables cover confounding. The stated aim is to let clinicians judge credibility and to help researchers report and discuss their studies for a clinical audience.

problems.evidence: Three appraisal questions are given in a form a clinician can apply to a published paper, covering the question and target trial, the alignment of the three time points, and data coverage of confounders. It is a reader-facing checklist rather than a dashboard, so it records whether the design was stated and not which of the resulting assumptions can be checked.
problems.quote: By evaluating (i) the clarity of the causal question and the specification of the target trial being emulated with observational data, (ii) the proper alignment of the time points for eligibility ascertainment, treatment assignment, and the start of follow-up, and (iii) the quality of the data and the extent to which available variables account for confounding factors, clinicians can make well-informed judgments on the credibility of target trial emulation results.

problems.evidence: The framework's contribution is located in reducing ambiguity about the causal question, which is a statement that the question was previously unclear and that stating it is the fix. Whether the stated target trial is the one the reader needs answered is a separate matter the appraisal does not reach.
problems.quote: As Hernán et al. stated, "the most impactful contribution of the target trial framework is the reduction in the ambiguity of causal questions because we cannot provide valid answers if we do not know what the question is".
problems.locator: Signal paragraph, should I trust the results

problems.evidence: The motivating problem is that critical care trials enroll a population that is neither the one most likely to benefit nor the one that receives the therapy in practice, which is offered as a leading explanation for their negative and unreplicated results. The same eligibility question determines who enters an emulation, and the viewpoint raises it as a reason to use observational data rather than as something the framework settles.
problems.quote: One of the leading hypotheses is that the eligible and included population in critical care trials is not representative of the population that might benefit most from the therapy, or does not reflect the target population that is most likely to receive the therapy in real-world clinical practice.

papers.title: Comparative Effectiveness Research Using Randomized Trials and Observational Studies: Validity and Feasibility Considerations.
papers.one_line: Separates internal, construct and external validity across trial and observational designs, and states that a true intention-to-treat analysis is not feasible in an emulation, that finding a no-treatment comparator is a major challenge, and that claims show a prescription was filled but not that it was taken.
papers.what_was_done: The review positions double-blind trials as optimizing internal validity and construct validity through prespecification and standardized collection while sacrificing external validity, pragmatic trials as improving generalizability at some cost to internal validity through open-label design, and observational comparative effectiveness studies including emulations as offering breadth and feasibility while lacking random assignment. Under internal validity it notes that variable selection for adjustment should follow theoretical models such as directed acyclic graphs informed by clinical experts rather than statistical criteria, that falsification endpoints partially alleviate concern about unmeasured confounders, and that claims data cannot capture prescriber and patient behaviors such as choices between therapies or no treatment. It states that a true intention-to-treat analysis is not feasible observationally, with an initiators analysis as a partial approximation and a sustained treatment effect analysis as an approximation of as-treated. Under construct validity it calls for computable phenotypes validated against chart review as ground truth, notes that trial-ascertained characteristics such as cancer staging or imaging parameters cannot be matched in claims, and that a filled prescription is not a taken drug. Under external validity it warns that some sources over-represent particular populations and that data provenance must be established.

future_research.gap: Evidence from randomized trials is often not durable, with the dual antiplatelet therapy example showing different results when reweighted to contemporary populations and technology.
future_research.quote:
However, subsequent analyses showed different results
when reweighted to represent contemporary patient populations and use of second-generation drug-eluting stent
technology.9

problems.evidence: The quantity a trial reports as its primary result cannot be produced observationally, and the two substitutes are named as approximations without any statement of how close they are. An initiators analysis and a sustained treatment effect analysis are different estimands from intention-to-treat and from as-treated respectively, and they are offered as stand-ins.
problems.quote:
Beyond these issues, true intention-to-treat analyses,
where participants are analyzed according to their assigned
treatment rather than actual treatment to provide conservative unbiased estimates, are not feasible in observational
CER studies.

problems.evidence: Constructing a no-treatment arm is named as a major challenge because of confounding and selection bias, so the comparison an emulation can actually make is between active treatments. That constrains which causal questions are askable, and the review states it as a standing limitation rather than something the framework resolves.
problems.quote:
Finding a suitable no treatment comparator group
is also a major challenge in observational CER studies that
follow the target trial framework due to concerns for
confounding and selection bias.

problems.evidence: Two construct-validity failures are stated plainly: a filled prescription does not establish that the drug was taken, where trials use diaries and drug-level testing, and clinical characteristics such as cancer staging or imaging parameters cannot be matched in claims or records at all. The remedy offered, validating computable phenotypes against chart review, addresses identification of conditions and not either of these.
problems.quote:
As for
outpatient drugs, claims data can tell us if a prescription
was ﬁlled but will not inform us whether the patient
actually took the drug.

problems.evidence: Falsification endpoints are offered as a partial remedy for unmeasured confounding alongside sensitivity and subgroup analyses, with the qualification that residual confounding remains possible. Instrumental variables are named as the technique that addresses both measured and unmeasured confounders and immediately qualified by the difficulty of finding an instrument meeting the assumptions.
problems.quote:
Sensitivity analyses and
subgroup analyses can help strengthen the robustness of
the results, and falsiﬁcation endpoints might partially
alleviate the concern for unmeasured confounders.

problems.evidence: Claims data are stated to be unable to account for the prescriber and patient behaviors that decide between therapies or between treatment and none, which is the mechanism generating the treatment pattern being studied. Those same behaviors govern what happens in the comparator arm over follow-up.
problems.quote:
For instance,
administrative claims data are often
unable to account for important patient and prescriber
behaviors, such as choices between various therapies or
no treatment, which could inﬂuence the observed ﬁndings.

papers.title: Comment on "Associations of semaglutide with first-time diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease in patients with type 2 diabetes: Target trial emulation using nationwide real-world data in the US".
papers.one_line: Letter identifying three failures in a published semaglutide and Alzheimer's emulation: comparator groups selected by indication in ways records cannot correct, unmeasured lifestyle and socioeconomic confounders, and an effect appearing within the first month of a disease that develops over years.
papers.what_was_done: The letter responds to an emulation reporting a 40 to 70 percent lower risk of first Alzheimer's diagnosis with semaglutide against other glucose-lowering drugs. Three objections are raised. First, prescribing is personalized: semaglutide is not first-line and is avoided in patients who are underweight, losing weight or have gastrointestinal conditions, while insulin is reserved for uncontrolled diabetes and catabolic states, so the insulin comparator group is systematically worse off in ways the analysis does not correct, and the relationship between body mass and dementia risk runs in different directions at different ages. Second, propensity matching cannot handle confounders that are not in the data: records rarely carry valid measures of diet or physical activity, only 7 percent of patients were recorded as having lifestyle problems although lifestyle measures should precede a semaglutide prescription, and socioeconomic status is poorly recorded while semaglutide users tend to be better off because of its cost. Third, Alzheimer's develops slowly with healthcare use rising 5 to 10 years before diagnosis and at least five years of follow-up recommended for prevention trials, yet a difference appeared in the first month and little effect after two years, which suggests selection or missing confounders rather than a drug effect.

future_research.gap: A sensitivity analysis excluding those diagnosed in the first year or two of follow-up would be needed to estimate any longer-term effect.
future_research.quote: We believe that a sensitivity analysis by removing those diagnosed with AD in the first year (even 2 years) of the follow-up would help to estimate the longer-term effects of semaglutide.

problems.evidence: The comparator arms are defined by drug class, and each class is prescribed under clinical rules that select on the outcome's risk factors: insulin marks uncontrolled diabetes and catabolic states, semaglutide is withheld from patients who are underweight or losing weight. The letter states the insulin group is the worst off in a way the analysis did not correct, so the contrast is between differently ill populations.
problems.quote: In other words, the insulin group is the worst‐off among studied cohorts in a way not fully corrected for.

problems.evidence: Two confounders that matter for both prescribing and dementia are absent from the records: diet and physical activity, evidenced by only 7 percent of patients being coded with lifestyle problems in a population where poor diet and inactivity drive the disease, and socioeconomic status, given that an expensive drug is used by better-off patients. Propensity matching on what is recorded cannot address either.
problems.quote: This seems likely because electronic health records (EHRs) rarely provide valid measures of diet and physical activity, which may be important confounders.

problems.evidence: An effect appearing in the first month for a disease whose diagnosis is preceded by years of rising healthcare use is not biologically interpretable, and the letter reads it as selection or missing confounding. The outcome is a recorded diagnosis rather than disease onset, so the timing of ascertainment is itself the exposure-related quantity.
problems.quote: Such “early effects” usually suggest a selection bias or missing confounders and, therefore, support our concern that the patient groups are not fully comparable.

problems.evidence: The letter's closing request is that the authors avoid causal language given the study design, in a paper whose title names the framework. The label is being used to license a causal reading that the letter argues the design does not support, and the correction has to be requested rather than being prevented.
problems.quote: Implementing the additional suggested analyses and avoiding using causal language due to the study design could bring new insights into the findings and strengthen confidence in them.

papers.title: A Post-Authorisation Safety Study of a Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine in Pregnant Women and Their Offspring in a Real-World Setting: Generic Protocol for a Target Trial Emulation.
papers.one_line: Generic emulation protocol for maternal RSV vaccine safety that enrolls women into a sequence of weekly trials by gestational age at vaccination, because administering a vaccine at 35 weeks makes a birth before 35 weeks impossible.
papers.what_was_done: The protocol evaluates a single dose of RSV vaccine given between 24 and 36 weeks of gestation against no vaccination, with vaccinated women matched to unexposed women on gestational age, calendar time, maternal age, immunocompromised status and high-risk pregnancy. Outcomes include preterm birth, stillbirth, hypertensive disorders, Guillain-Barre syndrome, low birth weight and small for gestational age, distinguishing those measured during pregnancy from those at or after birth. The primary outcome is preterm birth because regulators differ on the optimal gestational age for vaccination and a phase 3 trial of another candidate was suspended over preterm birth concerns. The design responds to a structural feature: vaccination at 35 weeks cannot produce a preterm birth below 35 weeks, so participants are enrolled into a sequence of weekly trials by gestational age at vaccination. Time between vaccination and birth is added as a continuous outcome with more power than the categorical one, allowing the median interval before preterm births to be examined and being independent of gestational age assessment accuracy. Outcomes are identified from code lists reviewed by clinicians with only narrow codes included, though preterm birth needs validation because spontaneous and medically indicated cases must be separated. Whether data sources capture RSV vaccination at all is uncertain because the programme is new.

future_research.gap: Whether current data sources capture maternal RSV vaccination accurately is unknown because the programme is new and national practice varies, and must be checked against national statistics before collection begins.
future_research.quote: Subsequently, it is essential to verify if the data source adequately captures this information and compare it with national statistics to ensure comprehensive coverage and prevent exposure misclassification in the comparator group.

problems.evidence: The protocol identifies a deterministic relationship between exposure timing and outcome possibility, vaccination at 35 weeks precluding birth before 35 weeks, and resolves it by making gestational age at vaccination the trial index, enrolling into weekly sequential trials. That is a design derived from the biology of the outcome rather than a convention, and it works because the relevant clock is gestational age.
problems.quote: For instance, administering the vaccine at 35 weeks of gestation cannot result in an preterm birth of less than 35 weeks. Therefore, we emphasise the critical importance of matching participants based on gestational age at the time of vaccination.

problems.evidence: A second outcome is added that is continuous rather than categorical, has more power, permits examining how long after vaccination preterm births occur, and does not depend on how accurately gestational age was assessed. Changing the outcome to remove a measurement dependency is a design move rather than an adjustment, and it is specific to this exposure and outcome pair.
problems.quote: Also, this approach allows us to examine the median time between vaccination and preterm births, which is crucial for identifying specific underlying mechanisms. For instance, it can reveal whether preterm infants are born days, weeks, or months after vaccination.

problems.evidence: The primary outcome cannot be identified correctly from codes because the target is spontaneous preterm birth and the codes do not separate it from medically indicated preterm birth, which is the case where the clinician acted. Validation is described as something that may be needed and as something to be done when resources allow.
problems.quote: For preterm birth, validation may be needed since preterm birth can either be spontaneous or medically indicated (iatrogenic), whereas our focus is only on spontaneous preterm birth.

problems.evidence: With only one approved maternal RSV vaccine the comparator is unvaccinated women, and the protocol flags that once other vaccines are approved the unexposed group will silently contain women vaccinated with a different product. The comparator's meaning is a function of the market at the time the study runs.
problems.quote: In the event that other RSV vaccines receive approval, it is crucial to consider their inclusion in the study design. This necessitates either incorporating all different RSV vaccines in the exposed group or excluding women specifically vaccinated with other RSV vaccines from the unexposed group.

problems.evidence: Fitness for purpose is named as something to be established in feasibility studies before the emulation runs, and a concrete check is specified for exposure capture: compare recorded vaccination against national statistics. The check is stated for one variable and the general condition is left as a pointer to feasibility work.
problems.quote: Data sources that routinely collect data often provide comprehensive information on treatments and outcomes but may lack sufficient detail on clinical factors that require adjustment [ 47 ]. Fitness for purpose of data can be assessed in feasibility studies [ 18 , 19 ].

papers.title: Conducting descriptive epidemiology and causal inference studies using observational data: A 10-point primer for stroke researchers.
papers.one_line: Ten-point primer for stroke researchers that states there is no consensus on when to prefer which adjustment method, and that meaningful sample size estimation is impossible for causal analyses of routinely collected data.
papers.what_was_done: The primer covers data types, biases, causal effect types, target trial specification, directed acyclic graphs, appropriate and inappropriate covariate adjustment, and estimation methods, with recommendations for researchers and reviewers. It distinguishes conditioning methods, regression, matching and stratification, from standardization methods, propensity weighting and g-computation, and sets out what each requires: conditioning assumes the causal effect is the same within every combination of observed confounder values, weighting depends on correct specification of the exposure model, and g-computation on correct specification of the outcome model. It notes that even with a correct causal diagram and covariate set there is no guarantee a single correct outcome model can be specified a priori, so several should be tried for g-computation. On positivity it observes that eligibility criteria imposed by the target trial framework increase the chance the assumption holds, and that violations make estimates unstable. A worked example study balanced 42 covariates only by linking several data sources. On per-protocol analysis it notes that adherence information is limited and sensitivity analyses can focus on those judged more likely to adhere. On power it states the database population differs intrinsically from the study population and only an unknown portion of the data is relevant.

future_research.gap: There is no consensus on whether or when any particular analytical method should be preferred.
future_research.quote: At present there is no consensus in the literature as to whether, and under what circumstances, a specific analytical method should be preferred.

problems.evidence: The primer sets out what each method assumes, shows the assumptions are not comparable, weighting needs the exposure model right and g-computation needs the outcome model right, and then states that the literature offers no basis for choosing. That is the absence of a defensible default written as guidance for a clinical audience.
problems.quote: In summary, all the discussed analytical methods rely on the same causal assumptions discussed in Point 3. What distinguishes them is that these methods rely on different statistical parametric assumptions, requiring correct specification of the model of interest, that is, whether the exposure or the outcome is being modeled.

problems.evidence: The primer states that sample size estimation is impossible in practice for these studies because the database population differs from the study population and only an unknown fraction of records bear on the question. Its recommended response is to report estimates with intervals and meta-analyze once enough databases have been used, which defers the power question to a synthesis that may never happen.
problems.quote: The discussions in Points 3, 6, 7, and 9 demonstrate that truly meaningful sample size estimation is impossible in practice.

problems.evidence: Positivity is connected to a design lever rather than left as an assumption: applying the target trial's eligibility criteria raises the chance it holds, since the criteria remove people who would never receive one of the strategies. The connection is stated qualitatively with no diagnostic and no statement of when the criteria are sufficient.
problems.quote: The application of eligibility criteria imposed by the target trial framework discussed in Point 6 increases the likelihood of fulfilling this assumption.

problems.evidence: The per-protocol analogue is recommended in addition to the primary analysis and immediately qualified as particularly challenging for want of adherence information, with the fallback being to restrict to people judged more likely to adhere on the basis of contact frequency. That restriction defines a different population and a different quantity from the per-protocol effect it stands in for.
problems.quote: This is particularly challenging in observational studies due to limited information on treatment adherence. To address this limitation, sensitivity analyses can be performed by focusing on a subset of individuals who are deemed more likely to adhere to the treatment protocol based on specific criteria.

problems.evidence: The worked example achieved balance on the 42 covariates a comparable trial would collect only by linking several data sources, and the primer states that secondary sources often do not carry the required information. The adequacy condition is thus set by what a trial would have measured, with linkage as the way to approach it and no threshold for when the shortfall matters.
problems.quote: This can be challenging in observational studies, particularly when utilizing secondary data sources which may not contain the required information.

papers.title: Comparative effectiveness of extended-release naltrexone versus buprenorphine-naloxone on treatment interruption: Comparing findings from a reanalysis of the X:BOT RCT and harmonized target trial emulation using population-based observational data.
papers.one_line: Harmonizes the design and analysis of the X:BOT trial and a Massachusetts administrative emulation, finds treatment interruption far more common in the real world, 82 and 93 percent against 68 and 72 percent, and a benefit for buprenorphine-naloxone visible only in the observational study.
papers.what_was_done: The X:BOT trial and an observational study using the Massachusetts Public Health Data Warehouse were analyzed with harmonized protocols and statistical methods, both estimating the 24-week risk of treatment interruption after inpatient medically managed opioid withdrawal for buprenorphine-naloxone against extended-release naltrexone. In the trial, reanalyzed risks were 68 and 72 percent, higher than the original report's 57 and 53 percent because the outcome and discontinuation definitions differ, interruption defined here as a medication possession gap over seven days. In the observational study the risks were 82 and 93 percent, consistent with other real-world reports. Buprenorphine-naloxone was favored by 11 percentage points observationally with an interval of 10 to 13, and by 4 points in the trial with an interval crossing zero, so the observational estimate lay inside the trial's interval and the discordance may be sample size. Only 12 percent of people in the observational cohort received either medication soon after discharge. The paper lists trial participants being more motivated, willing to be randomized, and paid 20 to 50 dollars per visit, which may have acted as contingency management, as reasons the absolute risks differ.

future_research.gap: Whether the displacement of heroin by high-potency synthetic opioids since the trial changes the comparative effectiveness of these medications is unknown.
future_research.quote:
Future research is needed to assess whether this development impacts the comparative
effectiveness of different MOUD, including methadone and extended-release buprenorphine
in addition to BUP-NX and XR-NTX45.

problems.evidence: Both studies were run with harmonized protocols and analyses, which is what a calibrated comparison requires, and the result is that they agree on the risk difference while disagreeing on the absolute risks by 14 and 21 percentage points. A binary concordance verdict would record agreement and lose the finding that the same treatment strategies interrupt far more often outside a trial.
problems.quote:
We found that for both treatment strategies, the risk of treatment interruption was
substantially higher in the observational study, representative of the real-world population of
Massachusetts, than in the target trial, a multi-site clinical trial in the US.

problems.evidence: Four candidate explanations for the divergence are listed, trial participants being more motivated, willing to be randomized, paid per visit in a way that may have functioned as an intervention, and seen by different providers at different frequencies which could be effect modifiers. None is quantified and nothing separates them from residual confounding, so the discordance cannot be attributed.
problems.quote:
Differences in patients who enroll
in trials, sample size, emulation differences, and residual confounding may have contributed
to these randomized-observational discrepancies.

problems.evidence: The reanalysis of the trial produced higher risks than the trial's own report because interruption replaced non-completion and a seven-day possession gap replaced discontinuation. Two definitions of the same clinical concept move the reported risk by more than ten percentage points within the same dataset, before any comparison across data sources.
problems.quote:
The higher risk in our re-analysis can be explained by differences in the
definition of the outcome (treatment completion in the original report versus treatment

problems.evidence: Twelve percent of the observational cohort received either medication soon after discharge, so the emulated trial is built from a small and self-selected slice of the eligible population. Preference for a treatment and willingness to be randomized are unrecorded in the administrative data and are exactly what distinguishes trial participants.
problems.quote:
Participants in X:BOT were also
willing to be randomized to either BUP-NX or XR-NTX whereas in the observational data,
we had no data on treatment preferences or willingness to be randomized in a clinical trial16.

problems.evidence: Harmonization was imperfect at a specific point: the trial randomized during inpatient withdrawal management and the administrative data do not record what medication was prescribed during that admission. The moment of assignment in the trial is unobservable in the emulation, so the two designs cannot be aligned there however carefully the rest is matched.
problems.quote:
For example, X:BOT patients were
randomized during inpatient MMOW, while information on MOUD prescribed during
inpatient MMOW was unavailable in the PHD.

papers.title: A New Target from a Target Trial Emulation: Allow Early Assisted Breathing.
papers.one_line: Reviews an emulation comparing early against delayed switching from controlled to assisted ventilation in 1,489 patients, and identifies the well-defined intervention as the most important unresolved challenge because switching was operationalized as any of several different clinical events.
papers.what_was_done: An emulation asked whether promoting assisted breathing earlier speeds ventilator liberation or prolongs respiratory failure by aggravating lung injury. Eligibility required at least two calendar days of invasive ventilation, no neuromuscular blockade and an oxygenation ratio above 150; assignment happened at whichever came first, a switch to assisted ventilation giving the early arm or 24 hours elapsing giving the delayed arm. Early switching was associated with a 7 percentage point higher rate of successful extubation and four fewer ventilated days. The commentary works through three challenges. The misalignment between eligibility and assignment creates immortal time because patients who die before switching can never enter the early arm, addressed by clone-censor-weight so that deaths occurring while assignment is still ambiguous are not counted against one arm. Confounding is partly handled by adjusting for driving pressure, oxygenation, extrapulmonary organ failure and sedation depth, with local sedation and weaning practice unmeasured. The third and most important is that switching was defined as any of transitioning to an assist-only mode, lowering the set respiratory rate below the spontaneous rate, or letting the spontaneous rate exceed the set rate without adjustment, so what a clinician should do to obtain the benefit is ambiguous.

future_research.gap: Which strategies best promote assisted breathing, how to trade earlier liberation against harm from excess respiratory effort, and whether benefit varies by cause of critical illness are all unanswered and need a trial with protocolized interventions and ventilator waveforms.
future_research.quote: These questions could be addressed by a randomized controlled trial with protocolized interventions and comprehensive baseline data, including ventilator waveforms.

problems.evidence: The commentary states the consequence exactly: because a switch was defined as any of several distinct clinical events, and those events may have different effects, the result does not tell a clinician what to do. This is the equivalence-class problem in a setting where the trial version of the intervention would be a protocolized change to ventilator settings, sedation or both.
problems.quote: This results in ambiguity in what clinicians ought to do to achieve the observed benefit of early switching, as the various ways of achieving a switch may yield different—beneficial or even harmful—effects.

problems.evidence: A 24-hour window separates eligibility from assignment, and cloning with censoring and weighting is used so that deaths occurring while a patient could still belong to either arm are not attributed to one. That handles the arithmetic correctly and leaves the window length itself unexplained, since a different grace period would define different strategies.
problems.quote: This misalignment between study eligibility and treatment assignment is a potential source of immortal time bias, as patients who die before switching to assisted ventilation can never be assigned to the early switching arm.

problems.evidence: The unmeasured determinants named are specific and clinically decisive: sedative agent and dose, the patient's overall trajectory, and local approaches to sedation and weaning that differ between centres and affect both the switch and the extubation. The commentary notes the authors had limited data on these, with no bias analysis bounding them.
problems.quote: Local approaches to sedation and ventilator weaning affect transitions to assisted breathing and the timing of eventual extubation ( 7 ); as the authors observe, they had limited data on this and other practices that may have differed by center.

problems.evidence: The commentary states that emulations benchmark well against trials when the design can be faithfully replicated and the data support confounding control, which makes the credential conditional on two things a reader cannot verify from the label. The study it is discussing then fails the first condition on the intervention definition, by the commentary's own account.
problems.quote: Observational studies that use target trial emulation have been shown to benchmark well against randomized trials when their design can be faithfully replicated and when the data source supports adequate control of confounding ( 5 ).

papers.title: Cancer publications using real-world data from the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database: Conceptual framework and bibliometric analysis.
papers.one_line: Classifies 1,232 cancer papers published from one national insurance database between 2006 and 2022 by design and method, finding propensity score use rising from 2.4 percent in 2011 to 40 percent in 2022 while exposure change over time remains an unresolved challenge.
papers.what_was_done: A framework combining study-based components, aims, design and statistical method, with disease-based components was applied to 1,232 cancer articles using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database. Annual publication counts rose from 15 or fewer before 2011 to over 120 by 2021. Risk factors were the most studied aim at 52 percent, followed by outcomes at 36 percent and incidence or prevalence at 3 percent, and risk-factor papers carried the highest impact factors. Among risk factor and outcome papers, 85 percent were cohort studies and 10.7 percent case-control, with propensity score use rising from 2.4 percent in 2011 to 40 percent in 2022. Attrition is described as negligible because insurance covers more than 99 percent of the population, but changes in exposure over time, particularly medication use, remain a challenge. Eight of the ten most cited articles examined whether a treatment for one disease was associated with altered cancer risk. The review notes that case-control studies drawn from this database should generally have been nested case-control studies, because a plain case-control design leaves it uncertain whether cases and controls come from the same source population, giving as an example the seventh most cited article which drew controls from a separate random sample.

future_research.gap: Handling change in exposure over time, particularly medication use, remains an unresolved challenge for studies of cancer risk factors in this database.
future_research.quote: Changes in exposure over time, especially with medication use, remain a challenge in studies examining cancer risk factors using the NHIRD.

problems.evidence: The dominant question in this literature is whether a medication changes cancer risk, and the review states that change in exposure over time is an unresolved challenge for exactly those studies. Defining what counts as being on a drug over years of follow-up is the operative decision in 52 percent of the papers surveyed, and it has no settled treatment.
problems.quote: Among cancer risk factors, clinicians were particularly interested in the association between medications for a disease and subsequent cancer risk.

problems.evidence: The review finds that many case-control studies in this database should have been nested within the cohort, because otherwise it is uncertain whether cases and controls come from the same source population, and gives a highly cited example that drew controls from a separate random sample. Comparator construction is failing in a way that is visible from the published design and was not caught.
problems.quote: Hence, whether the cases and controls are representative samples from the same source population is uncertain. 30

problems.evidence: Propensity score use grew from 2.4 to 40 percent of studies over eleven years without any corresponding change in what the method is applied to, which shows a method being adopted by diffusion rather than by demonstrated fit. The bibliometric framing records the method used and not whether the choice affected the result.
problems.quote: In both study designs, the use of the propensity score method increased steadily from 2.4% in 2011 to 40% in 2022.

papers.title: Causal inference from observational data in neurosurgical studies: a mini-review and tutorial.
papers.one_line: Tutorial for neurosurgical researchers that recommends specifying the causal question and target trial before study inception, and names three fixable habits: ambiguous treatment timing, mingling design with analysis, and the absence of a prespecified protocol.
papers.what_was_done: The tutorial moves from Bradford Hill's criteria, criticized as implausible, vague and lacking a strict definition of causal effect, to the potential outcome framework and directed acyclic graphs, then treats confounding and selection bias and surveys estimation methods with a simulation example. Its central recommendation is to define the causal question, conceptualize the randomized trial that would answer it, and design the observational study as an emulation. Three limitations of observational data are presented as removable by acting early: ambiguity about treatment timing is resolved by recording when treatment decisions were made, mingling of design and analysis is mitigated by withholding the outcome until treatment groups are balanced, and the absence of a prespecified protocol is addressed by writing one with the planned methods and steps. On method choice it advises propensity-based methods where diseases are rare and covariates many, notes they help identify and address positivity violations by excluding extreme scores at the cost of power and a changed target population, prefers standardization when the outcome model is better understood, and targeted maximum likelihood when neither is. Variables believed related to the outcome should enter the propensity model and those related only to exposure should be excluded. Dynamic treatment regimes are named as the extension real practice requires.

future_research.gap: Fixed treatment comparisons do not match clinical practice for relapsing and chronic disease, and evaluating dynamic regimes from longitudinal observational data requires attention to time-varying confounding.
future_research.quote: However, real clinical practice often involves individualizing and adjusting treatments based on patients’ characteristics and evolving disease status when dealing with relapsing and chronic diseases.

problems.evidence: The absence of a prespecified analysis protocol is listed as a standing feature of observational work in this field, alongside simultaneous access to covariates, treatment and outcome. Both mean the design that inference conditions on can be adjusted after the data are seen, and the tutorial's remedy is a recommendation to write the protocol first.
problems.quote: Another common limitation of observational study is the lack of a pre-specified protocol for analysis [ 2 , 9 ]. This can be addressed by establishing a rigorous protocol in advance and specifying the planned statistical methods and analysis steps.
problems.locator: Thinking causal inference as grounds before study inception

problems.evidence: The propensity score's advantage for positivity is that extreme scores can be identified and dropped, and the tutorial states the cost directly: power falls and the analysis sample no longer matches the target population. The estimand changes as a side effect of a diagnostic response, with no rule for where to cut.
problems.quote: For example, observations with extreme scores may be excluded from analysis to obtain more efficient estimates. However, discarding data may result in power loss and sample differences from the target population [ 55 ].
problems.locator: Choices along the causal inference process

problems.evidence: Estimator choice is presented as depending on which model the investigator is more confident specifying, propensity methods for rare diseases with many covariates, standardization when the outcome model is trusted, targeted maximum likelihood when neither is. That is a rule keyed to the analyst's subjective confidence rather than to any checkable property of the data.
problems.quote: When researchers have greater confidence in correctly specifying the outcome model rather than the propensity model, standardization can be a superior choice.
problems.locator: Choices along the causal inference process

problems.evidence: Missingness is classified by whether it depends on exposure or outcome, with complete-case analysis unbiased under the most restrictive condition and imputation or weighting under the next. Nothing addresses missingness driven by the visit process itself, and the recommendation ends at sensitivity analysis under each mechanism.
problems.quote: Furthermore, sensitivity analysis is needed to evaluate the robustness of conclusions under each missing mechanism [ 32 ].
problems.locator: Choices along the causal inference process

papers.title: Adjusting for selection bias due to missing eligibility criteria in emulated target trials.
papers.one_line: Shows that excluding patients whose eligibility-defining variables are missing, standard practice in record-based emulations, can overstate effect sizes by up to 10 percent, and supplies an inverse probability weighting correction for sequential emulations with time-to-event outcomes.
papers.what_was_done: Determining who is eligible is the first step of an emulation, and in electronic health records the variables defining eligibility are frequently missing because they are collected in the course of care rather than on a schedule. Patients with incomplete eligibility data are almost always dropped, or their eligibility is imputed from their most recent value even though that may not reflect current status. The paper proposes a conceptual framework for the resulting selection bias tailored to time-to-event endpoints under a sequence of target trials, with estimation and inference by inverse probability weighting, extending prior work that addressed a single trial with a continuous outcome by multiple imputation. A simulation infrastructure built to reflect the complexity of records characterizes the settings where the bias arises. Applied to bariatric surgery and microvascular outcomes among Kaiser Permanente patients with severe obesity and type 2 diabetes, failing to account for selection bias overstated effect sizes by up to 10 percent, and estimates were sensitive to the lookback windows chosen for body mass index and blood glucose, in some cases as sensitive as to whether selection bias was addressed at all. Imputation was infeasible here because eligibility would have to be imputed for 50 to 85 percent of subject-trials.

future_research.gap: Combining weighting with imputation may be needed for nonmonotone missingness in eligibility-defining covariates alongside missing confounders and outcomes, and has not been developed for this setting.
future_research.quote:
Combinations of IPW and imputation have been
used to address missing data in other contexts64,65 and may offer a
f lexible path forward for dealing with nonmonotone missingness
in eligibility-defining covariates as well as simultaneous missingness in other variables such as confounders or outcomes.

future_research.gap: No general rule exists for judging how large the selection bias might be for a given design or question.
future_research.quote:
It is impossible to give
a general rule of thumb for the degree to which selection bias may
or may not be an issue for any arbitrary study design or causal
questions.

problems.evidence: The framework is built precisely for the case where eligibility cannot be ascertained for everyone, and it names the two current practices, exclusion and carrying forward the most recent value, as unexamined sources of bias. It supplies a correction under a missing-at-random condition and quantifies the cost of ignoring the problem at up to 10 percent of the effect size.
problems.quote: In practice, patients with incomplete eligibility data are frequently excluded from analysis6 despite the possibility of selection bias.

problems.evidence: The correction rests on a missing-at-random assumption that the paper says is untestable and identifies its likely violation exactly: when the eligibility criterion is itself a measure of how sick a patient is, and sickness determines how often they appear in the record, the factor driving missingness is the missing variable. CD4 count in HIV and glomerular filtration rate in kidney disease are given as instances, and the method cannot reach them.
problems.quote:
In such hypothetical cases, sicker patients would likely
be overrepresented in the analysis population in a manner not
directly addressable by our IPW method, because the factor driving the missingness would, itself, be missing.

problems.evidence: Eligibility is assessed over a lookback window before each trial start, and the estimates moved with that window's length, in some cases by as much as the entire selection-bias correction. The window is a free parameter set by the analyst and it competes in magnitude with the bias the paper is correcting.
problems.quote: In some cases, differences between effect estimates using the longest and shortest lookback windows were on par with differences between estimates accounting and those not accounting for selection bias.

problems.evidence: Because a sequential design requires eligibility to be established repeatedly over time for the same person, every assessment is another opportunity for the eligibility variable to be missing, and the paper states the selection bias is potentially worse here than in other designs. In the application 50 to 85 percent of subject-trials had unascertainable eligibility.
problems.quote:
Given the need to ascertain eligibility for individuals repeatedly
throughout time, the problem of selection bias is possibly of
greater concern in the sequential TTE design than in other stud

problems.evidence: The paper's framing is that the framework's road map, which is credited with forcing researchers to think through design decisions, does not include missing data in eligibility criteria at all. A step that changes the estimate by up to 10 percent sits outside the checklist that studies are appraised against.
problems.quote:
Unfortunately, missing data, particularly missing data
in eligibility defining criteria, are not part of this road map.

papers.title: Concordance between randomized controlled trials and target trial emulation: A meta-analysis
papers.one_line: Meta-analyzes 82 emulation and trial pairs published from 2010 to 2025, finding a Pearson correlation of 0.55 overall rising to 0.86 in the 38 pairs with closer emulation designs, and systematic underestimation of treatment effects for venous thromboembolism.
papers.what_was_done: A systematic review and meta-analysis identified 82 pairs in which an observational study explicitly emulated a target randomized trial, published between 2010 and 2025. Concordance was assessed by Pearson correlation between the paired estimates and by a summary relative odds ratio, and factors associated with replication success were examined by regression and subgroup analysis covering emulation design, population characteristics and outcome definitions. Across all 82 pairs the correlation was 0.55 with interval 0.38 to 0.69 and the summary relative odds ratio was 0.99 with interval 0.94 to 1.03 and heterogeneity of 66 percent. In the 38 pairs judged to have closer emulation designs the correlation rose to 0.86 with interval 0.77 to 0.92. Concordance was impaired by differences in baseline age and sex between the emulation and the trial, by treatment initiation during hospitalization, and by poor quality of outcome emulation. Subgroup analysis found systematic underestimation of the treatment effect for venous thromboembolism, relative odds ratio 0.76 with interval 0.59 to 0.98, and for major adverse cardiovascular events, 0.93 with interval 0.89 to 0.97. The conclusion is that improving baseline population alignment, outcome ascertainment and multi-source linkage would raise replication success.

future_research.gap: Emulation design, particularly baseline population alignment and outcome ascertainment, needs improvement before replication can be relied on.
future_research.quote:
Improving emulation
design, particularly in baseline population alignment, outcome ascertainment, and leveraging multi-source linked databases, can enhance replication success.

problems.evidence: This puts a number on how far replication success transfers: a correlation of 0.55 across 82 pairs means agreement on any single new question is weak, and the three named impairing factors are properties of the emulation rather than of the method. The 0.86 for closer designs is a within-sample subgroup finding, so the higher figure describes pairs already judged well matched rather than predicting a new one.
problems.quote:
Among the 82 TTE-RCT pairs, the Pearson correlation
coefficient was 0.55 (95% CI: 0.38 to 0.69) and the summary ROR
was 0.99 (95% CI: 0.94 to 1.03, I2 ¼ 66%).

problems.evidence: Concordance is reported as a correlation and a relative odds ratio with heterogeneity rather than as a count of pairs that agreed, which is the calibrated comparison a binary label cannot give. The summary ratio of 0.99 conceals both the 0.55 correlation and the outcome-specific bias, showing that one aggregate agreement number is not enough on its own.
problems.quote:
Subgroup
analysis showed systematic underestimation of treatment effects for
venous thromboembolism (ROR ¼ 0.76, 95% CI: 0.59 to 0.98,
I2¼36%) and major adverse cardiovascular events (ROR ¼ 0.93,
95% CI: 0.89 to 0.97, I2¼19%).

problems.evidence: Poor quality of outcome emulation is one of three factors that significantly impair concordance, and the two outcome families showing systematic underestimation are venous thromboembolism and major adverse cardiovascular events, both composite endpoints assembled from codes. How the outcome is ascertained is therefore driving the discrepancy independently of the treatment effect.
problems.quote: Factors impairing concordance included differences in baseline age and sex, treatment initiation during hospitalization, and poor outcome emulation quality (p < 0.05).

problems.evidence: Treatment initiation during hospitalization is identified as impairing concordance, which is the setting where the moment of eligibility, the moment of assignment and the start of follow-up are hardest to separate because everything happens inside one admission. The finding is empirical across 82 pairs and no design rule follows from it.
problems.quote: Current real-world trial emulations demonstrate moderate concordance with corresponding RCTs.
